overall: Tomorrow (Saturday, June 20) is expected to be mostly sunny in Atlanta with only a slight 20% chance of afternoon showers or thunderstorms between 3–4 PM. The NWS official forecast pegs the high near 86°F, a modest cooldown from today's observed high of 89.6°F. forecast_obs_notes: There is substantial model spread for tomorrow's high. This ~6°F gap between the global dynamical models and the blend/NWS is a meaningful divergence and a key source of uncertainty; the full ensemble expected TMAX of 80.3°F versus the forecast-only model's 86.4°F highlights the same split.
max_temp_prediction: The ensemble probability distribution is broadly spread and bimodal, with the two highest-probability buckets at 78–79°F (14.9%) and 82–83°F (14.8%), consistent with the ensemble expected TMAX of ~80°F — meaningfully below the NWS/NBM target of ~86°F. Both prediction tier sets are rated Tier 4 (Poor signals, expected accuracy ~32%), reflecting this high uncertainty. A best-estimate of roughly 83°F balances the lower ensemble guidance against the warmer NWS/NBM anchor, but confidence is low; the realistic range spans approximately 79–87°F.
